summary: Arthur Venis was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford (B.A. c. 1874–1878). He served as Professor of English (1881) and Principal (1885, 1888) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and taught Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (c. 1888–1914).

Arthur Waley was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge (1907–1910), under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi. He served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. c. 1900–1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (c. 1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall studied at Wellington College (c. 1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (c. 1869–1874), later teaching Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who was educated at the University of Calgary (c. 1989–1993) and McGill University (c. 1993–2000). Around 2002, she became an Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.
Aruna Haldar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She held a teaching post at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (c. 1948–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He was a Sanskrit professor at MS University of Baroda (1967–1980) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard Divinity School. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976), the University of Sydney (1980), and was appointed Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill University in 1994.
Aryadeva was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was associated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning.

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held multiple leadership roles at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, including Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy (c. 2003–2009), and was attested as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973) and served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Asen Balikci was an anthropologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University (1956). He held positions at the National Museum of Canada (c. 1957–1964) and the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (c. 1965–1970), later serving in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his degrees at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, later heading philosophy departments at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the East-West Center (c. 1964–1969) and founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University (c. 1956–1958). He served at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Pune University, and as Professor of Applied Linguistics at Deccan College (c. 1967–1989).

Ashutosh Mukherjee was educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (B.A. c. 1880–1883). He held posts at the Calcutta High Court (1904), served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1906–1914), and was President of The Asiatic Society (c. 1907–1915).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is an Indologist and historian who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (c. 1964–1967). He served as a lecturer in English at Jangipur College and a Senior Research Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), the Academy of Finland, and served as Professor at the University of Helsinki (c. 1982).

Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist who studied at St. John's College, Selwyn College (1919–1922), and SOAS University of London (1922). He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.
